brief: JPM's Market Intelligence call says resilient growth, strong earnings, favorable post-midterm seasonality, and light retail participation support further equity upside. Leadership stays concentrated in AI and mega-cap technology, but election clarity, lower yields, or earnings beats could broaden the rally into small caps. The main risks are renewed food and energy inflation, another Fed hike, and any AI capex pullback. Oil has shifted from panic to fatigue, so diesel, not crude, may now be the bigger inflation signal, with conviction building in agriculture and food inflation into Q1. Extreme Nasdaq-versus-Russell positioning signals concentration. Sidelined retail buyers and heavy bond ETF demand could fuel a small-cap squeeze if bearish Russell positioning reacts to lower yields or midterm policy clarity, though the final two weeks before the election matter more than today's positioning. For earnings, AI capex guidance matters more than headline beats, surprises could emerge in financials, industrials, healthcare, and consumer, and rising input prices could pressure margins into 2027. JPM's own menu still likes Tech as a core long without an RTY short hedge, favors Banks ex-AI on a growth reboot, and flags a US/Iran deal as the catalyst to squeeze EU and Russell higher.
